Fixed in `tokio/src/sync/batch_semaphore.rs:376`.

**Cause:** the semaphore packs its state into one `AtomicUsize` — permit count in the high bits, a `CLOSED` flag in bit 0. `forget_permits` read the whole word, shifted right by `PERMIT_SHIFT` to get the count, subtracted, then wrote back `new << PERMIT_SHIFT`. That reconstruction dropped the `CLOSED` bit, so after `close()` any `forget_permits` call cleared the flag: `is_closed()` returned false and `try_acquire`/`poll_acquire` started handing out permits again. (`add_permits` was unaffected — it uses `fetch_add`, which leaves bit 0 alone.)

**Fix:** OR the observed closed bit back into the CAS target:

```rust
let closed = curr_bits & Self::CLOSED;
self.permits.compare_exchange_weak(
    curr_bits,
    (new << Self::PERMIT_SHIFT) | (curr_bits & Self::CLOSED),
    AcqRel, Acquire,
)
```

Since the bit is taken from `curr_bits` — the same value the CAS compares against — a concurrent `close()` between the load and the store loses the CAS and the loop retries with the fresh state.

`forget_closed` now passes; full `sync_semaphore` (18), `sync_semaphore_owned`, `sync_mutex`, `sync_rwlock`, `sync_mpsc`, and the in-crate `sync::` unit tests all pass.
